headline: Cursor ties trojanized Claude Code extension to a stolen Fireworks AI key; Check Point and UnrealIRCd KEV deadlines hit 11-16

bullets.text: New: Cursor says a stolen Fireworks AI key led to the trojanized Claude Code extension incident (The Hacker News). Fireworks is now a developing situation across 3 outlets, alongside Uber's report that driver licenses were stolen via Fireworks AI.
KEV deadlines arrive tomorrow, 11-16, for two exploited flaws: UnrealIRCd CVE-2026-114713 (server-level command injection) and Check Point CVE-2026-123039.
Check Point PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-123039, 4 outlets): attackers gain root on gateways, plant a backdoor and deploy a VMware ESXi wiper.
SCKit remains the top story at 8 outlets: worm-like malware aimed at MSPs that abuses ScreenConnect to deploy remote access and target technician sessions. Microsoft has published details.
Still active: the SignDrop Windows zero-day giving SYSTEM privileges (3 outlets), and Trezor's confirmed crypto-stealing implants in wallets sold via CryptoBilis, with a fix released.

Apache httpd CVE-2026-119618 remains open. KEV due 11-24: Cisco BroadWorks CVE-2026-20320, Openwave CVE-2026-111793, Outlook CVE-2026-124194, Chromium CVE-2026-125350. Last 7 days run 1.16x the 90-day average.

actions: Cursor and Claude Code users: review installed extensions against Cursor's disclosure and remove any you cannot verify.
Rotate any Fireworks AI API keys and review their recent usage for activity you do not recognize.
UnrealIRCd: patch or take internet-facing servers offline for CVE-2026-114713 before 11-16, and check them for injected commands.
Check Point: apply the vendor fix for CVE-2026-123039 before 11-16, restrict management access, hunt for backdoors, keep ESXi backups offline.
ScreenConnect: inventory instances and extensions, review technician sessions and hunt for SCKit using Microsoft's guidance.
Patch Apache httpd for CVE-2026-119618 and queue BroadWorks, Openwave, Outlook and Chromium before the 11-24 KEV due date.
